content:
Today I went to take pictures around town for the first time in months. I spent about 2 hours walking around till I finished what was left of the roll that was on my camera. It was chilly but there was some nice sun, and I got to take some nice shots. I hadn't been able to simply because I had no time to. I didn't really plan it, the day was nice so I just went for it.

It was a great experience, more so than usual. It was a meditation of sorts. This week wasn't particularly stressful, I didn't even have to go to the office. But I once again got too much into my own head about a bunch of stuff, and was a bit overwhelmed at myself.

I kinda wanted to buy some new shoes, kinda wanted to buy a new phone (again), kinda wanted this and that. I'm not really the type to spend money at all really. But when it's time to I must do all the reseach possible to get the absolute best option. This is a huge and stressing time sink that gives me a lot of desicion fatigue, but in the end I usually make smart purchases. The problem is when it's stuff I kinda want but don't particularly need. Sure I could use a new pair of shoes, haven't bought ones in 3 years or so, but the ones I have are still nice and functional so what gives. Sure I could upgrade my phone that was a midrange 7 years ago. Camera's not really up to par anymore, kinda laggy and worst of all some banking apps have straight up stopped working. But it's still functional, so what gives? 

Recently I bought a new fancy widescreen monitor. I spend a bunch of time looking at every possible alternative, and whether I really wanted/needed an ultrawide, but in the end the ultimate motivator was the fact that the monitor I'd been using for 4 years now bit the dust for some reason, and I really needed a new one. 

What I'm getting at is that I have a hard time buying stuff that I don't absolutely need, and by 'need' I mean I don't already have something that fullfills that purpose. I bought a watch and a camera, which I never really 'needed' but are still nice to have, and I'm really glad I made those purchases.

What I'm getting at is that this week's been just that. Stressing myself over purchases that I don't really need, doing a ton of research and having huge decision fatigue (heard it at work the other day and it's now my favourite term) and ultimately wasting my time doing that instead of doing the things I actually want/need to do. In the end I didn't end up buying anything. Kinda had the 'they're making me wanna buy shit that I don't need' moment. Sidenote, fuck modern phones. Everything's the same, they're all boring. There are so many kinda similar but also different companies and models that really fucks with my minmaxing brain. We should go back to Blackberries. But I digress.

Going around town on my own reminded me how much I love being on my own too. Like I said it felt like a meditation. I was just in the moment, going around looking for beauty in the mundane. It helped that I went to parts that didn't have many people around, cuz one thing I really don't like is being along around people that aren't (more on that another time).

I think I should strive more to be alone. And I don't mean alone as in hermit style cabin in the woods (although that doesn't sound bad) but more like disconnected. Disconnected from things that cloud my mind: ads, opinions, social media, you get the idea. I just redownloaded Medito to pick meditation back up and also downloaded a bunch of new books to my Kindle, we'll see how that works out. 

I think meditation is also gonna help me get in a better state to actually think of the major job/life decisions I need to make short-term. But I also decided I need to get better sleep, so that's gonna be reserved for a different time.
